title: Couple a scaffold transom to a ledger: lay it at its chalk mark, close the cap, swing the bolt in and run the nut down
instruction: Fix the transom to the ledger with the coupler at its chalk mark: lay it in, close the cap, put the bolt in the slot and run the nut down.
context: O*NET lists this task for Construction Laborers (47-2061.00): 'Erect and dismantle scaffolding, shoring, braces, traffic barricades, ramps, or other temporary structures.' A tube-and-coupler scaffold is built coupler by coupler. Each one is closed and bolted by hand, many times a day, before it is tightened. Here a right-angle coupler is already tightened on a ledger, its upper half open, and a 3.1 kg transom is to be fixed in it at its overhang mark. The steps differ, and they work a device through its own mechanism. First, lift the transom's near end while its far end turns on its bearer, and lay the tube in the open half with the chalk mark at the ledger. Then swing the hinged cap over the tube until it falls shut, swing the T-bolt up into the cap's slot, and spin the nut down until it bears. A coupler closed off the mark leaves the boards bearing short. In the demo, the right arm lays the transom and works the bolt and nut, and the left arm shuts the cap and holds it.
setup: Two YAM arms at the near edge of a table; positions are (x forward from the arm bases, y left) in cm, heights above the table. The ledger: a galvanised 48.3 x 4.0 mm steel tube, 60 cm long, along y at x 36, its axis 3.5 cm up, on two wooden blocks (7 x 5 x 1.1 cm, clamped to the table) at y -24 and 24. On it at y 0, an EN 74 class B right-angle (double) coupler: its lower half already tightened on the ledger; its upper half open above, with its saddle for a tube along x (axis 9.3 cm up, 5 cm wide). The cap hinges on the upper half's left side and lies back on its hinge, open 120 degrees. On the right side, the swing T-bolt rests outward on the ledger, about 12 degrees below level, with its nut 10 mm (5 turns) short of bearing; the model's bolt is M12 with a 19 mm nut, where a bought coupler has a 21 or 22 mm nut. The far bearer: the same tube, 40 cm long, along y at x 80, its axis 4.5 cm up, on two wooden blocks (7 x 5 x 2.1 cm, clamped) at y -15 and 15. The transom: the same tube, 70 cm long, 3.1 kg, with a white chalk band 15 cm from its near end. Its far end lies across the far bearer near y 0; its near end is at (20, -20), resting 10 cm in from the end in a wooden cradle (3 cm along the tube, 6 cm across, 8.9 cm high, a 90 degree V notch on top), set on the table. It lies 18 degrees off the coupler's line, clear of the coupler.
scoring: Read from video and an inspector's check. In simulation the coupler grips when its nut has been run down to bear on the cap; in a real trial the nut bears when it turns no further by fingers, and the coupler grips when, besides, a 50 N pull along the transom does not slide it. 1.0 when the transom lies in the coupler's upper half with its chalk mark within 10 mm of the ledger's near face (overhang 150 +/- 10 mm), square to the ledger (within 3 degrees), the cap is shut (within 3 degrees), the bolt is in the cap's slot, the coupler grips, and both hands are at least 6 cm from the coupler, all held for 1 s; until it has held 1 s it scores 0.5. 0.5 when the transom is at its mark with the cap shut and the bolt in its slot, without the 1.0 result (in a real trial, also when the pull slides it). 0.25 when the transom lies in the coupler's upper half at its mark. 0 otherwise. 0 also if the transom falls to the table, or if the coupler is closed with the mark more than 30 mm off.
reset_notes: Undo the nut 5 turns, swing the bolt out to rest on the ledger, and lay the cap back on its hinge. Lift the transom out, rest its far end on the bearer and its near end in the cradle. Nothing is consumed; the ledger's half of the coupler stays tightened.
fidelity: Rigid bodies at 240 Hz on GPU. The coupler is one articulation: cap and bolt on hinges, the nut sliding and turning on the bolt; its parts collide with each other and the transom. The thread is code, 2 mm a turn (a real M12's is 1.75), the nut stopping on the cap after 5 turns. The podger's final torque (about 50 N m) is left out. The nut is 19 mm, not EN 74's 21 or 22 mm, which rubbed the cap's ring. The cap is on the left; couplers fit either way round.
